title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: expanded controls for local AI agents
summary: The briefing accurately separates Microsoft's planned local-agent protection from existing Endpoint DLP controls. The roadmap facts, licensing background and monitoring instructions are supported; the policy-creation path only needs the category and regulation headings added.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the planned local-agent Endpoint DLP feature or its supported agents, operating systems and interaction points.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Endpoint DLP local AI agents supported operating systems preview list January 2027. Opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about, dlp-configure-endpoint-settings and local-agent-discovery-overview; no feature-specific coverage found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The local-agent control's default and any automatic change to existing policy behaviour on arrival are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "local" "agents" "default". Read the roadmap and endpoint-dlp-learn-about; no default or automatic policy transition for this feature was stated.

claims.claim: Local AI agents run on the user's device.
claims.quote: Local AI agents run with user-level permissions and can access files, tools, and services on the devices where they operate.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and devices
claims.claim: Existing Endpoint DLP supports Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) extends the activity monitoring and protection capabilities of DLP to Windows 10/11, macOS (the three latest released major versions) devices, and Windows certain server versions.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and devices
claims.claim: Existing Endpoint DLP supports macOS devices.
claims.quote: macOS (the three latest released major versions) devices

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and devices
claims.claim: Existing Endpoint DLP also supports certain Windows server versions.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP allows you to onboard devices running Windows Server 2019 and later versions.

claims.claim: Devices must be onboarded to use Endpoint DLP.
claims.quote: You need to onboard all the devices you want to use as locations in your DLP policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: An Updated policy sync status confirms that the device received the latest policy version.
claims.quote: If the status is Updated, the device successfully received the latest policy version.

claims.claim: Other sync statuses require investigation and do not by themselves mean that no policy is enforced.
claims.quote: This device isn't synced the latest policy updates. It might take up to 2 hours for the status in the devices list to update. Follow the steps in the workflow diagram to address issues.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated which account or component evaluates interactions for the planned local-agent Endpoint DLP protection.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Endpoint DLP local agent interactions block notification override evaluating component identity. Opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about and dlp-configure-endpoint-settings; no feature-specific evaluator stated.

claims.claim: How a local-agent DLP block appears to the person or agent is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Endpoint DLP local agent interactions block notification override evaluating component identity. Opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about and dlp-configure-endpoint-settings; no feature-specific block experience found.

claims.claim: Whether override is offered for the planned agent actions is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Endpoint DLP local agent interactions block notification override evaluating component identity. Opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about, dlp-configure-endpoint-settings and New-DlpComplianceRule; no local-agent override behaviour documented.

claims.claim: Existing Microsoft DLP guidance recommends incremental deployment using simulation and a pilot group before full enforcement.
claims.quote: Always take an incremental approach to deploying a policy, starting from the least impactful DLP simulation mode through full enforcement. ... Policy should be scoped to target a pilot group and then expand the scope as you tune the policy

claims.claim: Microsoft has not yet documented how that deployment guidance applies specifically to the planned agent controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview "local agents" "simulation" "roles". Opened dlp-create-deploy-policy and endpoint-dlp-learn-about; no local-agent deployment procedure or simulation support stated.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview policy-creation route reaches the Devices location for an existing Endpoint DLP policy.
claims.quote: Select the Custom from the Categories then Custom policy template from Regulations. Select Next. ... Accept the default Full directory under Admin units. ... Scope the location to only the Devices location.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].ui.path and the corresponding rendered path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom policy > Devices'. The cited page names Categories and Regulations as the headings for those choices.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <String> -EndpointDlpLocation <MultiValuedProperty> creates a DLP policy with Endpoint DLP user scope.
claims.quote: The EndpointDLPLocation parameter specifies the user accounts to include in the DLP policy for Endpoint DLP when they are logged on to an onboarded device. You identify the account by name or email address. You can use the value All to include all user accounts.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: Per-device policy sync details are available at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding > Devices > device.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices. ... Select a device to open the details pane for more information on the policy sync status.

claims.claim: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" retrieves Endpoint DLP device data through Advanced hunting.
claims.quote:
DeviceInfo 
| where DlpInfo != ""
| project DlpInfo

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second row and following prose
claims.claim: The DeviceInfo automation is a read-only Advanced hunting query in the Microsoft Defender portal, not a policy-changing operation.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Defender portal ... Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting ... Query the DeviceInfo table ... Expand the DlpInfo column to view Endpoint DLP device details

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first row and following prose

claims.claim: Policy delivery to devices is necessary for applying policy updates, making sync monitoring relevant after changes.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device. ... Devices must be online for the policy update to happen.
